description: A live, automated, technical field that outsiders keep treating as a museum piece. Ask about the floor, the tolerances, and the gap between the process document and what actually runs.

questions.text: What does the process document say, and what does the line actually do?
questions.lands_because: The gap between documented and actual process is where all the real knowledge lives, and everyone on a floor knows it exists.

questions.text: Can you hear when something is wrong before the instruments say so?
questions.lands_because: Sensory expertise is real on a floor and delightful on audio. It also opens the broader question of what happens to that knowledge as sensors replace it.
followups: Is that being lost as the equipment gets smarter?

questions.text: Tell me about a line-down. What actually happens in the first hour?
questions.lands_because: High-stakes, concrete, time-bounded, and expensive by the minute. Uses native vocabulary, which immediately establishes that you know the world.
followups: Who gets called, in what order?

questions.text: Where is the real tension between the floor and the office?
questions.lands_because: The defining social structure of a plant. Whichever side the guest sits on, they have a detailed and rarely solicited view of the other.
followups: When has the other side been right?

questions.text: What automation has actually worked in your plant, and what got quietly rolled back?
questions.lands_because: The rollback half is the question nobody asks. Failed automation projects are common, instructive, and rarely discussed publicly.
followups: Why did it fail - the technology or the implementation?

questions.text: What quality problem have you seen shipped because the schedule won?
questions.lands_because: The core ethical pressure of production work, asked concretely enough to produce a real answer rather than a policy statement.
questions.avoid_if: The guest holds current quality authority at a named employer and the answer could create liability.
